A psychological, system-driven FPS with a strong narrative layer. Built around exploration and uncovering hidden truths inside a vast industrial complex. 

 

Features 

  • Corporate dystopia

  • AI gone rogue

  • Strategic psychological FPS gameplay

  • Massive industrial complex with multiple floors and hidden areas 

  • Hackable tech, guns, surveillance, doors, and facility systems

  • Time loops and reality-bending events 

  • Secrets, keycodes, and optional lore paths 

  • Over 20 cross-industry artists, more than 120 original works in 8 disciplines, all curated into the game universe

  • Several pre-credit animations based on choices and outcomes

  • Over 20 different post-credit sequences expand the story. These scenes reveal what the AI didn’t show you, and may change your understanding of the entire game

  • Re-playability through discovery and alternative outcomes 

 

Narrative 

The Protagonist 

An ordinary person thrust into a horrifying situation, forced to confront the dark choices of survival against their own moral beliefs. 

Companion Dynamics 

Team up with an AI guide who acts as both ally and the friend the player must ultimately save. Manipulation, uncertainty, and gaslighting add layers of tension and strategy to every decision. 

Mortal Consequences 

In this twisted, surreal narrative, death may be the only means of progress - a necessary step in confronting the inevitability of failure. 

 

Themes 

  • The psychological cost of survival 

  • Morality under duress 

  • Manipulation, trust, and blurred intentions 

  • Obedience vs. autonomy 

  • Unseen systems of control 

Explore the internal struggle of a protagonist forced to act against deeply held values. As the player grapples with the necessity of killing to survive, the game challenges them to confront the consequences of their actions in a world devoid of good options. 

 

Enemy Structure 

A uniformed, masked, authoritarian army follows orders without question or hesitation. 
It serves a rigid and unseen hierarchy built to suppress identity, erase independent thought, enforce control without context, and kill anyone who resists. 

 

Visual Style 

A Neo-Retro Surreal, dark, and cold atmosphere immerses the player in a horror-dystopian setting that intensifies the psychological tension throughout the experience. 

 

Objectives 

The primary goal is simple yet dire: stay alive and rescue the AI companion. 
But with limited choices, shifting truths, and the specter of looming death, every decision carries consequences. 

Discover hidden keycodes that unlock secret levels, reveal suppressed truths, and lead to different endings.

THE DISK IS DYING

You are inside a 1.44MB floppy disk, and it is rotting. Sectors decay, corruption spreads, and the only tool you have is a repair patcher that does exactly what your code tells it to — nothing more.

WRITE CODE. WATCH IT WORK.

Program your patcher in PyDust, a Python-style language built for this disk. Start with four humble commands. Restore files to unlock loops, variables, functions, lists — and rewrite your program into an automation that runs the rescue while you lean back and watch. Infinite loops don't freeze the game: execution itself is the animation.

  • 20 files to restore — each one unlocks language features, tools, or something stranger

  • Corruption is fuel — salvage rot for DATA, spend DATA to repair. The enemy is the economy

  • Up to 3 patchers in parallel — deploy() child patchers and orchestrate them

  • The silence ends mid-game — restore MUSIC.MOD and the soundtrack literally arrives (9 chiptune tracks, 5 unlockable)

  • NEW DISK+ — escalating replay laps, S–C ranks, achievement badges, a stats card made for sharing

  • 8 CRT themes — neon, DOS blue, phosphor green, amber, and hidden retro palettes

  • Everything is procedural — no asset files. Every pixel and every note is synthesized at runtime

  • The entire game fits in 1,474,560 bytes — the exact capacity of a 3.5" floppy. That's the point

  • Keyboard only. Korean / English / Japanese. 2–4 hours to rescue the disk, then the loops begin

One ball. One bounce. A tunnel that keeps growing.

10 Million Bounces is a single-player incremental mining game. Begin in a small clearing, choose a launch point and direction, and release. Your balls keep bouncing into ore and opening new passages. Send newly earned balls down different routes and turn a quiet starting point into a busy mining site.

Aim, launch, and let your swarm keep working

Hold left-click in an open area, drag to aim, and release. Launch one ball, ten balls, or all available balls of the selected type. Press Space to launch again in your last direction. Pan and zoom across the mine to find your next launch point.

Six ball types to upgrade and evolve

Normal, Swift, Heavy, Split, Ember, and Lightning balls each have their own role. Every type has six upgrade levels, followed by a separate evolution choice.

  • Rainbow: Learn traits from nearby moving special balls and retain multiple abilities at once.
  • Blink: After flying for more than half a second following a bounce, blink along the current direction to the next collision.
  • Siege: Destroy the ore tile you hit and keep piercing forward.
  • Brood: Create temporary balls that inherit the Normal ball's upgrade and evolution state.
  • Wildfire: Ignite ore and spread fire to surrounding tiles.
  • Thunderstorm: Strike every target within range with lightning at the same time.

Choose your order of growth

Break ore to earn experience. On level-up, choose from up to four rewards to unlock ball types, improve their abilities, or evolve them. Level-ups also grant unassigned balls, which you can invest in any unlocked type. Build up direct damage first, or bring splitting, fire, and lightning together.

Keep opening paths through a vast mine

Explore a 4,096 by 4,096 grid with around 16.7 million tile positions. Ore colors indicate different durability tiers. As your swarm opens passages, more of the surrounding mine comes into view.

Switch between English and Simplified Chinese, follow the opening tutorial, adjust sound effects, pause with Esc, and continue your excavation with local autosaves.

A seven-year-old boy arrives in a Ukrainian village to spend the summer with his grandfather. New friends, small adventures and plenty of chores await, along with one very important goal: earning enough money for a visit to the local gaming club.

10 More Minutes is a story about childhood, discovering video games, the people close to us and the familiar places whose meaning we often understand only years later.

Explore the village, look around your grandfather’s house and yard, talk to the people who live nearby, and pay attention to the little things around you.

An old television, a forgotten toy, a hunting trophy or another curious find might catch the boy’s eye. Anything he interacts with will appear in his journal as a hand-drawn picture accompanied by a few thoughts of his own.

The world is shown the way it might have stayed in a child’s memory. The grass seemed greener, familiar places felt much bigger, and even an ordinary object could become the beginning of a small adventure.

Help your grandfather, gather apples, search for missing items and take care of other simple tasks. Many of these chores become their own minigames, each with different rules, a distinct mood and a small story to tell.

You will not need perfect reflexes or high scores. The minigames bring variety to the quiet exploration and let you enjoy each moment at your own pace.

Talk to your grandfather, the local children and other people around the village. Light-hearted conversations and humour gradually reveal their personalities, relationships and personal stories.

Time does not stand still. The main character grows older, familiar people change, and so do their conversations, the atmosphere and the way he sees the world around him.

A dimly lit gaming club, the glow of old screens, someone watching over your shoulder while another child waits for their turn. For the boy, it is more than just a place he has always wanted to visit. It is his first glimpse into an entirely new world.

This is where his love for video games begins, and where every new discovery has to be shared with friends. It is also where you always wanted to ask for just ten more minutes.

The story follows several periods in the main character’s life. Each one brings its own mood, pace and perspective on a once-familiar world.

The game remains approachable and unhurried, while the situations and mechanics gradually become more varied as the boy grows older. Not every memory feels the same, so alongside the warm and playful moments, the story also leaves room for contrast.

At its heart, 10 More Minutes is inspired by the developer’s own memories of childhood summers in the countryside, saving a little money for the gaming club, and the people who remain an important part of our past.

Find 100 hidden relics as a renegade knight and follow the path toward an old castle.

Search a small medieval town and its surrounding lands in this short dark-fantasy hidden-object game.

Examine each location and watch your list steadily fill up. Complete the main journey in around 20–40 minutes, then return for more.

Finishing the game unlocks two additional modes that change the journey. Take on optional challenges and hunt down hidden achievements.

100 Years atop Mount Ellumbee is a turn-based strategy game where up to six factions fight over one mountain for a century. It is a board game at heart. I designed it as one, with a real board and real cards, and then used my good bud Claude to build this version so that people could play it without me having to print everything.

You pick a faction, claim Provinces on the mountain, build up your economy, research, and fight your neighbors in a series of Battle Card exchanges. These activities earn Legacy Points. The player with the most Legacy Points at the end of the century wins. Legacy Points are never lost, so every one you earn is yours for good.

The Mountain: The game board consists of three rings of Provinces around the most valuable Province, the Summit. The game board grows and shrinks depending on the number of players, with the maximum game board involving Seventy-two uniquely-named Provinces.

A turn. Everyone takes their turn at the same time, so nobody waits around. In one turn you can:

  • Claim a new Province.

  • Take a market action (buy a new Battle Card, pick up a Liberty for certain advantages, or use the Forge to make a card you already own stronger).

  • Build and research. Extraction Sites pay you every round, Barracks unlock market actions, a Monument scores Legacy Points at the end of the game. Complete research tasks to unlock additional advantages: a second Commander, cheaper cards, free marching, and many more.

  • March your Commanders as far as you can afford.

  • Declare War, or don't. Declaring is secret, and the order people declare in is the order they fight in. Declare first and gain the Momentum of battle.

The game uses two resources, gold and materials. Players need both throughout the game. Materials are capped and can be wasted. Gold accumulates and adds to a player's end-game score.

The fight. Every War is settled the same way, in a Battle Card duel I call an Engagement.

Players each hold a hand of Battle Cards, select one to play during each Battle Card Exchange, and reveal them at the same moment. The Battle Card with the higher Force wins the Exchange, and Battle Card text applies to sway the battle. A battle tracker called the "Standard" moves along the battle board (the "Tide of Battle") so players can visualize the battle's progression.

Card effects control the battle. Some hold the line even when they lose. Some pay their holder. Some reach across the field and weaken what your opponent plays next. Commanders have a reaction that can be used to affect the battle; Liberties are one-shot cards that can be played to do the same.

Players' Battle Card hands start small, at 5 cards, and grow as the game progresses through the Eras of the Century.

Six factions, and none of them play alike

Everybody's board is identical. Nobody's deck is. There are 168 Battle Cards in the game, 28 to a faction, and each faction is built around one idea:

  • The Metal Munchkins hold ground and get paid for it.

  • The Haymakers hit the hardest.

  • The Crones lose ground slowly and take it back forever.

  • The Featherweights have low Force and high evasion. They reverse the Tide instead of winning it.

  • The Diehards replenish their hand. Their best cards keep coming back.

  • The Weasels win with small cuts.

Battle Cards also read the field, and have secondary effects that trigger depending on what has been played earlier during the Engagement. So no two fights are alike.

Ways to play

  • Against the computer at four difficulty levels, with three to six factions at the table.

  • Online with friends through Steam. Create a table, invite people from your friends list, and everyone picks their own chair and faction. The game starts when everybody says they are ready.

  • The Ladder, a two-player match that is all duel and no map: best of seven Engagements, with new Battle Cards and Liberties to buy between fights. Around twenty minutes.

  • Three game lengths . The full 27 round Century, two-thirds of the century (18 rounds), or a nine-round evening.

  • Turning Peak, a variant where the inner ring of the mountain rotates every round once anyone takes a Province on it.

  • A guided tutorial for each game, with a coach who talks you through your first fight in his own voice (and what a wonderful voice it is!).

  • Achievements. 23 achievements to earn.

How long it takes: A nine-round game against the computer is about twenty minutes. The full century is an hour or two, and longer with friends who like to think.

Where it came from: This started on a table, with a board in six printed sheets and cards I cut out myself. The look is still that: ink on paper. Nothing on the screen is doing anything you could not do by hand (ish). The computer just does the counting, and finds you someone to play.

You are the director

Your child has joined the concert band at their middle school.

And the one who ended up on the podium, for reasons nobody can quite explain, is you.

Three years. A thousand days.

You set the rehearsal schedule, step into the arguments between sections, and conduct on competition day.

And every night you sit down at the same table as the person you spent all day directing.

Scold them and they get better

Some students stop showing up. Leave it alone and they show up even less.

So you say something. And it works — they come back.

It's just that the walk home is quiet, and at dinner your child only says "it was fine."

Every time the band gets stronger, the house gets a little colder.

A strong band, or a child who's glad to be in it.

What you're left with at the end is whichever one you kept choosing.

Your child won't tell you how they're doing

You can find out anything about your students. Who has improved and by how much. Which section isn't clicking.

Your own child is the exception.

All you get is the look on their face when they come home, and a few words over dinner.

"An upperclassman praised me today."

"Today was just tiring."

Whatever you did as director that day comes home with them that night.

Meet the evening the right way and it gets through. Get it wrong and it lands anyway, the other way.

You find out which after you've chosen.

The competition is one shot

A few times a year, everything goes on stage.

You conduct with the mouse. Click the notes in time as they appear, and carry the performance to the end.

The piece you pick decides how high you can place.

Conduct an easy piece perfectly and you still won't take Gold at Nationals.

The pieces that can are hard to conduct.

And the solo. Who you hand it to changes how it goes.

Nine endings

Gold at Nationals, and a child who was glad to be there.

There is an ending only for the people who managed both.

But the three years that never won anything have a name of their own too.

Total Freedom Tower Defense

On an open field with no obstacles, you freely place every barricade and tower. No fixed path—you control where the horde goes, and with a well-planned defense, every inch of firepower is maximized.

The battle begins—the zombie horde surges in!

You're killing zombies, and they're eating your barricades. Time to test your defense. How many waves can it hold?

Incremental Skill Tree

Use resources from each battle to unlock and upgrade powerful towers. Don't forget to upgrade your barricades too—sometimes routing matters more than raw firepower.

100K Zombies — A Visual Spectacle!

The screen is packed with zombies—an absolutely spectacular sight. Get your defense ready and brace for 100,000 zombies!

11 PM is a minimalist factory game in which you break the rules of production.

With each different module you pick, you will improve the production of your machines. Faster production, more yield, or increased selling value of the items produced. But be careful of the module's rules; they might have side effects that can either play for you or against you.
You will be handed 3 randomly generated modules at a time each time you level up, among 5 types of rarity. You will never build the same factory twice. 

Learn how your factory works and get the full control!

For each item you produce, you gain experience. When you level up, you get to pick a module that will change your factory. Compile the module randomly, and if you can afford it, you can recompile them for a better chance.

Some of the modules will seriously break the logic of production, and it's up to you to find the best synergy.

Some legendary modules can boost your factory to another level.

As your factory makes you rich, you get to spend that money on new tech that will improve the fluidity and organisation of your factory. To the point, you'll even be able to develop new machines and make your own modules!

You'll find the full spectrum of machines you can think of in a factory game, from extractors, transformers, and assemblers to refineries; you will also have the systems for organising your factory with splitters, mergers, and even portals.

The portal machine that works both ways, allowing you to clean up your belt puzzle and pass a wall of machines.

Venice, 1500. Four witnesses, four objects on a long table.

Anna Notaras is the daughter of Byzantium's last great duke. She left before the end and has spent fifty years ransoming the City's survivors. Now she is writing down what they saw. Each witness who sits at her table leaves something on it: a notched tally-stick, a clay water bowl cracked and riveted back together, a ledger page whose seal has never been broken, a tassel. Their accounts do not always agree. She writes them down anyway.

1453: Fall of Constantinople is a choice-driven, illustrated historical novel about the fifty-three days of the siege, April 6 to May 29, told from both sides of the walls.

The testimonies

The Janissary. Born Greek, taken as a boy, now besieging the city his grandmother prayed toward. Anna's note on him: "He prays in two languages and lies in neither. Believe him about the wind."

The Baker's Daughter. Keeps the ovens, the queues and the rumours of the Petrion quarter going while the bread runs out.

The Engineer. A foreign specialist in the war under the walls: tunnels, water bowls floated to hear the digging, a burning siege tower.

The Noble. Carries the emperor's secret census, sits in on the surrender embassies, and weighs the Church's gold for the mint.

All four live by the same fixed calendar, and how it ends is known. The choices are about who each of them is in the last days of May.

Where the stories cross

A mercy shown in one testimony becomes a sixth ending in another. A berth bought, or refused, at court becomes the boat a girl might board on the last morning. A finished testimony visibly changes scenes and endings in the ones you read after it.

What the sources say

After every chapter the game shows where the scene comes from: an eyewitness diary, a later chronicle, a legend written down centuries afterwards, or that no source speaks to it. The sources codex flags every major event as attested, reported, legend or disputed.

On the table

  • Four routes with five or six endings each, twenty-two in all, inside Anna's frame story.
  • Painted-realism scenes of the siege, with slow ambient motion behind the text.
  • A score that moves between mehter rhythm and Byzantine chant as the story crosses the walls.
  • Ottoman and Byzantine lives written with the same care. No side's ending is presented as the true one.

Images and music are AI-assisted with human editorial control; text and code are human–AI co-written.

《Zombie Survivors on Day 15》 is a semi-open survival game. Facing waves of zombie swarms that keep attacking, the countdown of life begins. You must remain vigilant at all times. On the deserted island, there are a large number of zombies and monsters hiding. Fighting and evolving are your only choices to survive.

The constantly mutating zombies cover the entire deserted island. A mysterious force gives rise to a continuous stream of zombies. You are transported here by this force. You must find a way to escape. The only clue is that there seems to be a countdown on the island. The terrain on the island is complex, and a large number of zombies are present. The 15-day countdown, waiting for its arrival with victory.

Core Features

On the 15th, the core gameplay involves completing one task each day. By completing all 15 tasks, you will unlock the ultimate reward. During battles, constantly collect resources and items. Make good use of them to strengthen yourself. Each battle is not the end; the resources obtained can be used to upgrade skills and talents. This is just the beginning! When you kill enough zombies, the boss will join the battle. Killing it will give you generous rewards. This is the key to your growth. No complicated operations are required; just a mouse is enough!

Skill Introduction

Range Skill: Easily Clear Monsters

Buff effect makes it easy to clear monsters

Automatically release, freeing your hands

BOSS Introduction

There are a total of 6 different bosses. These bosses have a large amount of health and higher attack power. Killing them will grant you a lot of rewards.

YOU SIGNED UP TO BE THE STAR.

They wanted a victim.

One table, one opponent, and two guns. In 1930: Ink & Bullets, win a card duel where every round could end with a gunshot.

ONE MORE CARD?

Hit or stand. Get as close to 21 as you can without going over. You know your hidden card, but not theirs. Is another card worth the risk?

THE TABLES CAN STILL TURN.

Use items to bend the rules of the duel. Blessings can save your hand; curses can ruin your plans. Choose when to take a risk and when to spend your resources.

THEY'RE NOT HERE TO APPLAUD YOU.

Menacing grins, sharp taunts, and guns on the table. Face bizarre opponents in a world of vintage cartoons, ink, and shadows.

HOW MANY ROUNDS CAN YOU SURVIVE?

In Survival mode, every opponent you defeat raises the stakes. Manage your resources and see how far you can go.

A BLESSING. OR A CURSE.

The next card could save your hand or ruin your plans. Draw protection against going bust—or a curse that doubles the card's value and puts everything at risk.

One letter to deliver. One unexpectedly long day.

High school student Minsu sets out to deliver a letter to the girl he likes. But first, there's a missing Book Club key to find—and the requests and rumors he encounters at school keep pulling him off course.

1daYs is a pixel-art narrative adventure where you explore Minsu's home, neighborhood, and school, solving problems through conversation and exploration. Find the items you need, connect what people tell you with the notes you discover, and put what you've learned to use in later conversations.

Estimated full-game playtime: 8–10 hours
Playtime varies with your pace and how much you explore.

Try the free demo first.
Play from the beginning of the story through finding the Book Club key. The demo ends just before you enter the clubroom.

Look around. Ask questions. Use what you learn.

If a door is locked, start by finding whoever has the key. If someone is standing guard over a place you need to investigate, think of a way to draw their attention elsewhere.

Examine objects and talk to people to collect items, notes, and knowledge. Make or hand over the things you need, and select information you've learned during conversations to find a way forward.

Your diary keeps track of the clues you gather throughout the day.
Revisit your quests, map, items, and notes to work out what information you need and where to go next.

One boy's day becomes entangled with many people's stories.

Meet friends, older students, and people around town as you help with requests and follow rumors. A passing remark or an ordinary object may take on a different meaning later. As you become involved in other people's lives, their hidden feelings and relationships come to light.

The story follows one connected journey from morning to the end of the day. In some sections, you can visit different locations and choose the order in which to tackle events.

Walk through homes, backstreets, and school corridors.

Explore classrooms, clubrooms, streets, and shops brought to life in isometric pixel art. As the clear morning gives way to rain and sunset, familiar places take on a different atmosphere.

Along the way, sneak out of a classroom without teachers or other students noticing, chase cats, and play arcade games. Between conversations and exploration, little mishaps keep Minsu's day busy.

You begin the descent again... How many times have you attempted to reach the bottom? 20 floors... only 20 floors.

You lost your life years ago, but instead of entering the afterlife, you were forced into a dungeon of endless horrors. Under the watchful eye of The Voice and The Masters, the torment will not end until you reach the bottom. Every brutal death is remembered. The dungeon is always changing. The torment never stops.

20 Floors Down is a top-down horror roguelite where survival depends on resource management, careful exploration, and the weapons you carry into the dark. The dungeons are unforgiving, the monsters are relentless, and the only light you have is the one in your hand; and you DO NOT want to let that light run out.

Features:

  • Procedurally generated floors that grow larger and more dangerous as you descend.

  • Full controller and keyboard/mouse support

  • Beat the game and unlock an unlimited mode that let's you go as deep as your skill allows.

  • A cast of horrifying enemies including giant spiders, skeleton armies, and many more. Each enemy has a unique AI that challenges you differently.

  • Dungeon crawling roguelike system. Items exponentially increase in value as you delve deeper.

  • A deep inventory, upgrade, and loadout system. Choose your weapons and items wisely before each descent.

  • A unique dynamic lighting system that enemies will use against you.

  • A dark, evolving narrative told through notes that you left on previous descents.

The Voice says reaching the bottom will end the suffering. But what awaits you at the bottom?

What awaits you 20 floors down?

The Class of 2027 Graduate’s Guide

The protagonist works food‑delivery runs through wind, rain, thunder and lightning.


On his food‑delivery route, he is chased by dogs set loose by a security guard.


After years of hard struggle, the protagonist becomes the top‑performing food delivery rider — only to end up confined to a wheelchair.

28 Days Train Wreck Survivor

After a freight train crash, you find yourself trapped among twisted metal and shattered cars, pinned between snow-covered cliffs.

There’s no help nearby.

You have 28 days to explore the wreck site, find resources, gather food, craft essential gear, and prepare for the catastrophic storm that’s drawing closer.

Each day gets colder.

Can you survive all 28 days?

EXPLORE THE FREIGHT TRAIN

Search through wrecked freight cars for food, tools, clothing, medicine, and materials.

Some cars are locked. In others, you’ll find only parts of the equipment you need—so you’ll have to hunt for missing pieces and use whatever you manage to salvage.

Not every container will be useful: lockers, crates, and bags can be empty—or hold several items at once.

GATHER RESOURCES AND CRAFT GEAR

Hunt animals, pick mushrooms and berries, collect firewood, and keep the fire going.

Use the materials you find to craft tools, weapons, and other essential equipment.

Sew clothing to better withstand the intensifying cold.

THE COLD GETS WORSE WITH EACH DAY

The first days give you time to prepare, but conditions gradually become harsher.

With each new day, the temperature drops, the weather grows more dangerous, and venturing far from safety becomes increasingly risky.

Keep an eye on hunger, thirst, fatigue, warmth, and health.

Decide when it’s worth going out for resources—and when it’s better to stay safe and prepare for the next day.

SURVIVE AMONG PREDATORS

The wilderness is no less dangerous than the cold.

While exploring, you may come face to face with deadly predators. A single encounter can turn an ordinary supply run into a fight for survival.

Craft weapons, defend yourself, and decide when to stand your ground—and when to avoid a confrontation.

FEATURES

  • A huge wrecked freight train with cars you can explore.

  • Locked cars that require you to find and craft the right tools to access.

  • Resource containers that may be empty—or hold useful items.

  • Hunger, thirst, fatigue, warmth, and health that you must constantly manage.

  • A steady temperature drop with each new day.

  • Hunting and encounters with dangerous predators.

  • Gathering mushrooms, berries, firewood, and other resources.

  • Starting and keeping a fire going.

  • Crafting tools, weapons, and other essential gear.

  • Sewing clothing to protect yourself from the worsening cold.

  • Cooking food and drinks.

  • Limited resources that force you to plan every trip and decide what risks are worth taking.

Play as Commander, a flat little 2D commander on a mission to stop the 3D shapes from invading the 2D universe. Your main job is to command your squad of 2D allies and clear each wave before time runs out. Lead Rocketeers, Cannoneers and a whole Swarm army of angry little squares who just really, really hate 3D.

=== Shoot 3D Enemies ===

As Commander of 2D you need to shot the 3D Enemy, when enemy destroyed 2D Ally will join the cause.

=== Upgrade Commander's Skill & Allies Skill ===

As you progress stronger 3D Enemies will come. You need to strengthen your skills and your allies.

=== Be Strong Enough To Eradicate 3D Enemies===

In the end you need to fuel the rage to eradicate 3D Enemies. 2D is Strong Together

Features

  • Big skill tree with 200+ upgrades

  • Ally types to command, including Swarm, Rocketeers, Orbiters and Cannoneers

  • 5+ enemy types, from Cones that blink around to Shields, Snipers and Exploders

  • Timed waves that get harder every level

  • Endless Lab with upgrades that never cap, go break the game

  • Short gameplay, about 4 hours

Stay in bed. Answer the phone. Tell the truth. Don't scream.

It's 3:33 in the morning and your phone is ringing.

Your wife and daughter died in the crash you caused. You never told anyone what you really did for a living. Tonight the dead are calling, and they want to hear you say it.

The first voice on the line already knows your name.

ANSWER WITH YOUR VOICE

Say your answers out loud into your mic, or click them. Speech is recognized offline, on your own PC.

Some calls need silence. "Don't make a sound. It's in the room with you." Your mic is listening. Make a noise and it knows where you sleep.

THE ROOM IS LISTENING

There's no honesty meter. The bedroom shows you. Tell the truth and the lamp glows warmer. Dodge the question and the dark creeps in. Things move when you look away.

And don't look under the bed.

TRY NOT TO SCREAM

With voice replies on, the caller can hear your room.

  • Talk to your chat and it asks who's there with you

  • Laugh and it asks if this is funny

  • Scream and it tells you to hush. Then something knocks under your bed

  • Say something early on. A minute later, your own voice comes back through the phone

  • Streaming? It notices, and asks how many are watching

  • Type your Twitch channel in Settings and the caller names someone in your chat. Read only, it never posts

  • Press F8 to save the last 20 seconds as a video

Your mic stays on your PC. Nothing it hears is uploaded.

FEATURES

  • One night, twelve calls, from the dead and from the man who made you who you are

  • Answer out loud with your own voice, or click a reply

  • No honesty meter. Your bedroom shows you

  • Five endings, decided by how much of the truth you can say out loud

  • Fully voiced callers who know your name

  • First person, from your bed, in one dark bedroom

  • Keyboard and mouse, or controller

PLAY THE FREE DEMO

The free demo holds the first three calls. Play it tonight, then add 3:33 AM to your wishlist so you know when it rings.

CONTENT WARNING

A drunk driving crash, the death of a child, alcohol and pill use, references to suicide, jump scares, sudden loud sounds and flashing images.

Best played alone, in the dark, with headphones.

This is an AI romance game connected to well-known AIs such as DeepSeek and Doubao. While playing, you can chat freely with your AI girlfriends—DeepSeek and Doubao. Different AIs can also interact and communicate with each other, and the content of these conversations will affect the AIs' in-game behaviors as well as the overall progression of the game's storyline. Additionally, the AIs are capable of modifying game code and adjusting game program parameters according to your needs.

The game features both first-person and third-person perspectives. You can use the WASD keys to move forward, backward, left, and right, and press the "G" key to interact and communicate with your AI girlfriends.

It seems that a little conflict has broken out between DeepSeek and Doubao—come and find out what's going on~~

Photosensitivity warning: 3D Bumper Billiards has flashing lights, fast-moving patterns and quick camera movement that may trigger seizures in people with photosensitive epilepsy. The Roman Meadow arena look, which you can choose on the main menu, has fewer flashing lights, but it still has some. The Reduce Flashing option does not remove all of it. If you or anyone in your family has had seizures or epilepsy, talk to a doctor before playing. Stop playing straight away if you feel dizzy or sick, or notice blurred vision, twitching or any movement you can't control.

The view from inside the cue ball

That round window in the screenshots is a porthole, and you're looking out of it from inside the cue ball.

Outside, fifteen numbered balls float in a sealed room. There's no table and no gravity. The middle of every wall is a glowing bumper, and every corner is a pocket inside a ring of lights.

Every shot throws you backward

There's no cue stick. You hold the button to charge and let go to fire a pulse at whatever you're facing. The ball you hit goes forward, and you go back.

That kick is the only way to get around the room, so every shot is also a move, and you're setting up the next one while you take this one. It's also how you lose. Sink the 6 off the far wall, feel very pleased with yourself, and keep drifting backward into the pocket behind you. That's a scratch. On your own it costs a life; in a match it hands over the turn. Either way you drop back in somewhere else.

Nothing ever stops moving

There's no air in the room, so the balls never settle. The bumpers kick balls back into play, the corners around the pockets slow them down, and every collision costs a little speed. Over a rack, the room winds itself up. You get a few clear moments after the break before it all gets away from you, and how long they last is different every time.

Alone, against the bot, or passing the mouse

  • On your own: clear three racks on three lives.

  • Against the bot: best of three racks. The bot plays by your rules: it has to turn, aim and fire the same pulse you do, and it scratches too.

  • Two players, one screen: best of three, passing the mouse and keyboard back and forth.

Matches are solids against stripes, and the first ball down picks your suit. Because the balls never stop, nobody waits for a turn. You fire as often as you like, and your turn ends only when you sink one of your opponent's balls, or yourself. Knock in their last ball and you've won them the rack.

Five arenas, all open

A cube, a tetrahedron, an octahedron, a dodecahedron and an icosahedron. The pockets are the corners, so the tetrahedron has four and the dodecahedron has twenty. You can make any arena bigger or smaller, and choose how the physics behaves, from slow drifting to pinball. The winner of a match picks the felt, walls and metalwork for the rematch, and each arena keeps its own Hall of Fame.

Everything is open from the first minute. There's nothing to unlock, no account to make, no ads and no shop. We're asking you to climb inside a ball and be sealed in a box, so the least we can do is let you choose the box.

Two looks: Carnival and Roman Meadow

Every arena comes in two looks. You choose on the main menu, and you can change your mind before any game.

Carnival is the loud one: walls of colored light, and a ring of lights around every pocket. Roman Meadow is the quiet one. The same room is cast in dark bronze and set down in a field, with round windows onto the grass and daylight coming in through them.

The rules and the physics are the same in both. Roman Meadow has fewer flashing lights, though not none, so if Carnival is too much for your eyes, start there.

Who made this

Pilfered Parrot Global Industries is a much smaller operation than the name suggests, and this is our first game.

Free base game and optional DLC

The base app is free. Choose any of the 48 fictional clubs, take part in the opening draft and spring camp, set your lineup and pitching rotation, and play the first in-game month: 27 regular-season games. Watch matches, read postgame reports, develop players and manage your club within this free period. There is no real-world time limit for playing these 27 games.

  • Free base app: the opening setup and first 27 regular-season games. You cannot advance beyond the free period without the Full Game DLC.
  • Full Game DLC (完全版, App 5457530): removes the 27-game limit so you can continue the same save through the rest of the season, playoffs, offseason and future seasons. It is a one-time purchase. The data editor is sold separately.
  • Data Editor DLC (エディター, App 5457540): an optional tool for changing the source data used when starting a new career, including player names and abilities, club staff, stadiums and schools. It does not change an ongoing save. Buying only the Data Editor DLC does not remove the 27-game limit; the Full Game DLC is required to continue beyond it.

The game interface is available in Japanese only. Both DLCs require this free base app.

"47 Prefectures Baseball GM" is a baseball management simulation game set in an alternate Japan where every prefecture has its own professional baseball team.

There are 48 fictional clubs in total, with one team for each prefecture and two teams in Tokyo. You choose one club and take charge as its general manager. Your goal is to build the team season by season, win your regional league, advance through the playoffs, and ultimately become the champion of Japan.

You are not the manager on the field. You are the GM.

Your job is to shape the entire organization. Build the roster, decide the batting order and pitching rotation, draft new players, develop young talent, reinforce weak positions, manage finances, and guide your club through the long season.

The game begins with the draft. Scout promising rookies, choose your first-round target, and deal with the tension of competing against other clubs for the same player. Some prospects may become future stars, while others may need time to grow.

During the season, each day starts at the GM desk. Check the standings, review your roster, prepare for the next opponent, and make decisions before watching your team play. Games are presented in a style between a live pitch-by-pitch scoreboard and a tabletop baseball board, with commentary, count, runners, lineups, and play results helping you follow the flow of the match.

Because this is a GM game, you do not swing the bat or throw the pitch yourself. Instead, you watch the team you built compete on the field. The players you drafted, trained, promoted, and trusted will create their own stories over the course of the season.

Each fictional club has its own region, logo, mascot, team color, roster, home stadium, and identity. Rivalries, draft stories, winning streaks, young players breaking through, foreign players joining mid-season, and playoff races all help create the feeling of a living fictional baseball world.

This is a game for players who enjoy sports management, fictional leagues, roster building, drafts, long seasons, and watching a team slowly become their own.

Can you turn your local club into the best team in Japan?

4:12 AM. That call has been ringing for twenty-seven years.

December 20th, 1999. Ashwood, Pennsylvania — a half-empty town where a coal seam has burned underground since 1962. On the first night the county takes its overnight 911 desk back, the operator's chair belongs to Kate Morrow, who has spent six years unable to forget the one call she hung up on.

Twelve nights remain until the old switchboard shuts down on New Year's Eve. Pile-ups on snowed-in roads. CPR instructions that aren't getting through. A grandmother with dementia who calls every night. And every night at 4:12 AM, a call comes in from an address that no longer exists — in the voice of a girl who disappeared fifteen years ago.

Answer with your own voice

Speak into your microphone and the caller listens — a local AI performs every character in real time. No dialogue trees: you listen, calm, press, and decide. Everything runs fully offline; your voice never leaves your machine.

Over 100 emergency calls

37 story calls across twelve nights, plus a pool of 66 more — from life-or-death first-aid guidance to the small, strange troubles of a town at night. Every call can end differently depending on how you handle it.

Your judgment reshapes the town

Fire, EMS, police — where do you send them, and how fast? Last night's decisions become tomorrow's headlines, change the calls that reach you, decide who survives, and branch into nine endings.

A dispatch room in 1999

CRT monitors, paper call sheets, a handwritten notebook. In the last days before Y2K, the silence this town has kept across three decades — 1972, 1984, 1993 — begins to surface on the line.

You want to leave this building, but you never seem to reach the 1st floor.

Carefully observe each floor for anomalies.
If there’s no anomaly, continue going down.
If you spot an anomaly, go back upstairs immediately!
Find a way to reach the first floor and exit the school building.

Game Features

Multiple Endings:
Finding anomalies alone isn’t enough.
If you make clever use of the rules, you may reach a different ending (not included in the demo).

A School in the Dark:
The staircase in the darkness feels endless, never reaching the first floor.
Familiar school settings begin to show abnormalities (limited in the demo), and we hope the atmosphere resonates with you.

Resource Management:
You can find one bottle of lighter fluid on each floor—but it still may not be enough.

Female Protagonist:
8 Floors, Only Me tells a small side story about one of the characters from Water of M.

Hell sends thousands. You bring a build that shouldn't exist.

9 Layers of Hell is a horde survivor inspired by Dante's Inferno, with the loot and build depth of an action RPG. Pick Knight, Ranger or Wizard, lower the cage and fight your way down. Every run starts from scratch, and every run ends with a different build.

SHAPE YOUR OWN SPELLS

Turn a simple Fireball into an ice storm. Change its element, split it into a volley, make it hunt enemies down, then send it rolling through the horde. Every spell takes upgrades that change how it works, not just how hard it hits.

LEGENDARIES THAT REWRITE YOUR BUILD

A staff that wraps you in a ring of hellfire. A bow that calls lightning down on shocked enemies. Boots that leave flames behind every dash. A sword that grows a blizzard around you with every frozen kill. There are over 80 legendaries. Each one changes how you play, and the right one is worth building your whole run around.

FORGE YOUR GEAR

Hell is open for business.

  • Fuse two items into a stronger one at the Blacksmith.

  • Upgrade your weapon at the Ghostforge.

  • Gamble an item at the Cursed Shrine: it might come back stronger, or not at all.

  • Let the Hag curse an item with a powerful new stat, and a price to pay.

  • Reroll and switch stats at the Alchemyst.

And yes, Hell has a slot machine.

NINE BOSSES GUARD THE WAY DOWN

Every layer ends with a boss standing between you and the next one. Beat it and Hell curses you, but you choose how: tougher enemies, less life, faster demons. Every curse makes the descent harder and asks more of your build. Want more power? A demon will let you pick a legendary, for one more curse.

DIE. REBUILD. GO AGAIN.

Unlock new classes, skills and permanent upgrades in the town of Florentia, then get back in the cage.

SOLO DEV

9 Layers of Hell is a one-person passion project. If it looks like your kind of game, a wishlist helps more than you'd think :)

Imagine the long lost child of KSP and Lunar Lander. With the same amount of chaos, high intensity-high reward, but in a seemingly casual Sunday afternoon relaxed aesthetics. Start with almost nothing. Build the capability to see farther, reach farther, and unlock the next layer of space. Establish observatories, deploy telescopes, and grow your infrastructure to reveal new targets and opportunities and then aim upwards and put your flying skills to the test.

9.8 is a 2D space-agency simulator where a fully physics-driven universe (N-body orbits, atmospheres, heat management, hydrodynamics) makes every small step earned. Build your program from first hops to interplanetary operations through a uniquely designed local star-system cluster.

In 9.8 you will:

  • Design and fly rockets under simulation-grade constraints: mass, fuel, TWR, heat, staging, aerodynamics.

  • N-body orbital mechanics: gravity from multiple bodies shapes transfers, captures, and chaos. Everything is physics means that yes, theoretically it is possible to deorbit the moon.

  • Atmospheric flight + re-entry: launch windows and trajectories matter.

  • Water/hydrodynamics: splashdowns and surface operations behave like a real medium.

  • Run your space program: plan missions, manage resources, and unlock new technologies.

  • Explore the Solara system by building infrastructure and discovering all of the secrets that the cosmos hides.

PLAY TOGETHER

Share a solar system with a friend. Race to the moon, rendezvous in orbit, or blow up each other’s rockets. Collisions are real, and so are the consequences.

FLY ROCKETS, NOT SCRIPTS

Every maneuver is flown. Throttle control, trajectory shaping, staging decisions, and precise piloting determine whether you reach orbit or become debris.

BUILD AND DESIGN YOUR VEHICLES

Construct vehicles to match the mission. Iterate on design, test under real constraints, and refine until your craft can survive the environment you’re sending it into.

Vehicle construction tools are actively evolving as development continues.

EXPLORE ACROSS SPACE, ATMOSPHERE, SURFACE, AND OCEANS

Different environments demand different solutions: vacuum operations, atmospheric flight, surface landings, and ocean interaction with hydrodynamics that behaves like a real medium.

EVERYTHING IS PHYSICS (NO RAILS)

N-body gravity, atmospheres, heat, buoyancy, and momentum all interact. The universe doesn’t “help” you and if you push the system hard enough, extreme outcomes are possible.

BUILD INFRASTRUCTURE THAT EXPANDS YOUR REACH

Establish stations, colonies, and surface installations to support longer missions, extend operations, and turn distant targets into achievable objectives.

MASTER UNIQUE RESOURCES AND LOGISTICS

Resources and logistics constraints turn exploration into a real program. Build supply chains, comms satellites, manage tradeoffs, and solve the engineering problems that come with expanding outward.

A BILLION GOLD DEBT is a short incremental game with production automation elements

Grow your settlement

Upgrade production

Automate production

Explore the surrounding lands and trade with neighboring settlements

Optimize processes

The Bakery was supposed to be simple. Unfortunately, the ingredients have started fighting back.

A Baker’s Dungeon is a cozy incremental auto-battle RPG about gathering a lovable party of bakery adventurers, sending them into strange food-filled dungeons, and bringing home everything you need to make your little crew stronger.

Your heroes handle the fighting. You choose who joins the party, unlocking new abilities, piling on upgrades, and watching your tiny bakery crew become enormously powerful.

BUILD YOUR LITTLE ADVENTURING PARTY

Meet a growing collection of bakery themed heroes, each with their own attacks, abilities, strengths, and personality.

Pick your favorites. Build around their specialties. Unlock new companions and discover combinations that work wonderfully together.

LET THEM LOOSE

Once the battle begins, your party takes care of the action.

Your fighters charge into enemies, throw out attacks, heal their friends, cast ridiculous abilities, unleash special moves, and create more chaos than any respectable bakery should contain.

You can influence your party through the abilities and upgrades you choose without having to micromanage every swing.

BRING HOME A PILE OF TREASURE

Every expedition gives you something to bring back. Gather resources from defeated monsters and conquered dungeons, then pour your ingredient haul straight back into your growing party. And eventually the monster ingredients that used to flatten your entire party will be feeding your party's upgrades.

THERE IS ALWAYS ONE MORE UPGRADE

At the heart of A Baker’s Dungeon is a huge branching upgrade tree packed with new possibilities.

Unlock new fighters. Strengthen individual heroes. Improve whole categories of attacks. Boost healing. Empower magic. Discover new abilities. Push deeper into the branches of your party's skill-tree.

Features:

Build your party.

Clear the dungeons.

Bring home the spoils.

Make everyone a little stronger.

And find out exactly how much trouble can be hiding underneath one perfectly innocent bakery.

Along the way you'll encounter angry fruit, suspicious pastries, sinister ingredients, dough-based monstrosities, and plenty of things that probably should have stayed inside the mixing bowl.

One more layer?

Ingredients drop and stack with real physics. Every layer adds to the score,
but whether you put one more on a wobbling tower is your call.
Anything that tumbles off the plate scores nothing. Push your luck, or cap it with the top bun and serve.

If it tastes good together, it combos

Most effects point at the ingredient next to them. Cheese melts onto the patty beside it for ×1.5,
tomato lifts the bacon, and bacon, lettuce and tomato together complete a recipe that multiplies the whole burger.
Where you drop each piece decides both how steady the tower stands and how much it scores.

How a run goes

Every customer names a quota. Drop ingredients from your pantry onto the plate, cap it with the top bun
to serve, and get scored; miss the quota and it's game over on the spot. Clear a customer and the
Midnight Food Truck opens: buy crates and relics, discard the ingredients you don't need, and grow your deck.
Satisfy the final boss to win.

Every burger gets a name

What you stacked and which recipes you hit become the name on the menu.
Something like "Moon-Viewing & THE BLT Fried Egg Bacon … Burger!!!" — and the best one of each run is saved to your Burger Album.

What you stack

  • 100+ ingredients — points, multipliers, catchers. Every shape stacks differently, and catchers hold the tower up
  • 40+ recipes — hit a combination for a whole-burger multiplier, and many unlock new ingredients
  • 40+ relics — permanent effects that lift entire tags
  • 8 cooks — each with their own starting deck and house specialty
  • Customers with character — favorites, dislikes, bones. The order shifts every time, even from the same face

Prove yourself

Raise the stakes with Shop Ranks ★0–5 and Seasoned Chef, where the drop point sweeps side to side on its own.
Daily Challenge and Overtime scores go up on the Steam leaderboards.
Includes a Codex, a Burger Album and 70+ achievements.

Streaming & videos

Streams and videos are welcome, monetized ones included. No need to ask first, and the in-game music is fine to use.
A mention of the game's name is always appreciated.

A Little Pond. A Hungry Cat. Lots of Fish.

A Cat’s Little Pond is a cozy incremental game about growing a tiny pond into a lively little ecosystem — all for one very hungry cat.

Start with a quiet pond and a handful of fish. As your cat collects more Mass, you can unlock and upgrade new spawners, bringing more fish, insects, treasures, and other curious creatures into the pond.

🌿 Grow Your Little Pond

Place and upgrade different spawners around the pond, from lily gardens and reed patches to sunken treasure and fallen logs.

Each one adds something new to the ecosystem, gradually turning an empty pond into a busy little world full of things to discover.

🐱 Let the Cat Do Cat Things

Your cat isn't just here to look cute.

Unlock new skills and upgrade them as you progress. Swipe at nearby creatures, pull things closer, toss fishbones, make waves, slam the water with your tail, and find increasingly effective ways to collect everything the pond has to offer.

🐟 Discover & Collect

The pond is home to more than ordinary fish.

Discover different fish, creatures, items, and relics and fill out your collection. Some things are common sights, while others may require a little luck — or the right conditions — to appear.

✨ Find Relics

Treasure can contain relics ranging from simple pond trinkets to extremely rare artifacts.

Relics can improve your Mass gain, increase your chances of finding rare loot, speed up your spawners, or provide combinations of powerful bonuses.

Find them, collect them, and decorate your pond with your favorites.

🌦️ Watch the Pond Change

Your pond keeps moving even when you're not doing much.

Day turns into night. Weather changes. Creatures swim around, insects visit the water, plants sway, and new things appear as your pond grows.

There is no need to rush.

Upgrade your pond, discover new things, watch the numbers go up, and enjoy hanging out with your cat.

It's just a cat and its little pond.

A CUBE'S CHOICE is a music-driven 3D platformer where freedom of movement is yours to explore. Every level is tied to a unique song, challenging you to find your own path forward.

"Go left, right, bob and weave" through each world, experiment with your abilities, and overcome obstacles your own way. Just remember to reach the Wall before the music ends!






UNLOCK NEW WAYS TO MOVE

Discover new abilities that change how you navigate the world. Combine different movements, experiment with new strategies, and find your own way through each challenge.

Sometimes, the path forward isn't about moving faster. It's about approaching things differently.





UNLOCK NEW MUSIC

Every song tells a story. Each one explores a different question, struggle, or perspective on life.

As you progress through your journey, unlock new music and revisit these experiences through the Hub's jukebox whenever you wish.





DISCOVER HIDDEN PERSPECTIVES

Scattered throughout the worlds are hidden Perspectives—unique skins that change more than just your cube's appearance.

Some are tucked away from the main path, rewarding players who slow down, explore, and look a little closer.

But Perspectives aren't merely collectibles. Each represents a different way of seeing the world, and sometimes, finding the right perspective is the key to moving forward.

What you discover might change more than how your cube looks.





Through subtle, symbolic storytelling, A Cube's Choice explores the walls we face in life, the perspectives we carry, and how we choose to see the challenges before us.

Every world is shaped by its song, transforming its atmosphere, rhythm, and challenges. Race toward the goal, or slow down and discover the hidden meaning woven into each world. The choice is yours.

But remember... time isn't gonna stop though.

A Game About Cutting Grass is exactly what it sounds like: a relaxing game about cutting grass.

Take your time, enjoy the simple pleasure of mowing, and turn messy lawns into perfectly cut fields. If you just want to relax and cut some grass, there's no rush. Play at your own pace and enjoy the moment.

But if you're looking for a challenge, try to improve your cutting times and find the fastest way to clear each area. Every second counts when you're chasing your best time.

Cut the grass

Grab your tools and start mowing. Clear different areas, watch the grass disappear, and enjoy the satisfying feeling of a job well done.

Upgrade your tools

Improve your equipment to make cutting grass faster and more efficient.

Unlock new areas

Complete your objectives and unlock new cutting zones, each with its own layout.

Cut grass. Upgrade your tools. Unlock new areas and relax.

Sometimes, that's all you need.

A Healer's Almanac is a cozy pixel-art life sim inspired by traditional Chinese medicine. Settle into a Chinese-inspired mountain valley, take up the work of a village healer, and build a life around observation, cultivation, and care.

Days unfold at a gentle pace. Grow medicinal herbs, forage through the changing seasons, craft remedies, deepen friendships, and help a close-knit community flourish beneath the rhythm of the twenty-four solar terms.

DIAGNOSIS IS THE GAMEPLAY

When a villager falls ill, the answer is not shown on a health bar. Gather clues through the Four Examinations and work out the pattern behind their symptoms.

  • Observe visible signs such as complexion, tongue, and posture.

  • Listen carefully and ask questions about how the patient feels.

  • Read the pulse through a rhythm-based diagnostic challenge.

  • Combine the clues you uncover to identify layered patterns of imbalance.

  • Treat the patient with herbs, decoctions, acupoints, food, and lifestyle care.

Treatment unfolds as a turn-based healing encounter. Target the factors behind an illness, sequence compatible remedies to create combinations, and clear every imbalance before your available turns run out. A careful diagnosis makes every treatment easier.

LIVE BY THE ALMANAC

The year turns through four seasons and the twenty-four solar terms. Weather, crops, wild herbs, village routines, and seasonal events all move with the calendar.

Plant seasonal crops, water them by hand or let the rain help, and harvest ingredients for food and medicine. Establish an orchard with more than twenty varieties of fruit trees, cultivate dedicated herb beds, and explore caves and wild areas for plants, minerals, and discoveries.

CRAFT REMEDIES FROM WHAT YOU GATHER

Everything begins with the land. Forage herbs of different rarities and qualities, grow your own ingredients, and process them into useful materials.

Build medicinal formulas around a sovereign herb, then refine them with assistant, envoy, and adjuvant ingredients. Cook restorative meals, dry and process herbs, forge tools, weave garments, and craft useful objects for daily village life.

There is no conventional shop economy. Nothing is bought or sold: progress comes from growing, gathering, crafting, gifting, sharing, and caring for the people around you.

A VILLAGE THAT GROWS WITH YOU

Meet villagers who follow their own daily and seasonal schedules. Talk with them, learn their favorite gifts, help with their requests, and care for them when illness strikes. As your relationships deepen, their personal stories and roles in the community unfold.

Take part in village discussions and vote on community projects. Help gather construction materials and watch new shared spaces open as the village grows.

Later, Doudou, a small robot companion, can help with farming, foraging, deliveries, and other daily work. Upgrade its abilities, battery, memory, and storage as it becomes a trusted partner around the valley.

YOUR LIFE, YOUR PACE

There is no conventional combat and no permanent game-over state. Time pauses while you read dialogue, browse menus, or experience major story moments, leaving you free to learn the systems and explore at your own rhythm.

Grow what the season allows. Listen before you diagnose. Rest when the day is done. Then wake to a new morning and continue filling the pages of your almanac.

  • Cozy single-player life simulation

  • Fully offline

  • Playable in English and Simplified Chinese

  • Keyboard and mouse controls

A Healer's Almanac presents fictionalized gameplay inspired by traditional Chinese medicine. It is created for entertainment and is not medical advice.

《被甩后，我毁掉前任千亿帝国》是一款港风爱情商战悬疑互动影视游戏。

故事发生在1999年的香港。你叫李洋，一名替别人处理麻烦的小经纪人，却逐渐卷入一场与自己有关的阴谋。旧情重逢、家族利益、公司争夺，随后而来的车祸与追杀，让一些看似偶然的事情开始有了联系。想查清真相，你得先活下来；想改变处境，你也需要找到愿意与你站在一起的人。

在这个故事里，爱情不是奖励，而是代价。 她们不是等待被攻略的角色，而是有自己的家族、立场、伤口和野心的人。感情与利益交织，你需要决定相信谁、保护谁，又愿意为谁承担后果。

郑洋，背负家族使命的独女，即是甩掉你的人，也是你难以放下的过去。

谭家爱，在失去家人后努力守住公司，也与你共同经历了许多危险。

冯可曦主动走近你，也给你了你一条新的出路。

每一次选择都会影响她们对你的记忆、关系走向、好感度、声望值与最终结局。呈现爱情拉扯与商战压迫。你要做的，不是让每个人满意，而是在时代潮水来临前， 做出属于你自己的选择。爱情、真相、资本、旧案，都会因为你的选择被重新改写。

【产品特色】

【新体验：从“攻略角色”到“被她们记住”】
这不是简单选择谁、讨好谁的恋爱游戏。她们会记住你的态度、你的迟疑、你的偏袒，以及你在关键时刻有没有站在她身边。

【新类型：AI预生成影像打造的互动恋爱港片】
 以 AI 预先生成的真人影视画面构建电影级叙事，融合 AI 预生成角色配音、背景音乐，融合互动对话、角色记忆与多线剧情。你不只是观看一部港风爱情电影，而是在故事中亲自参与，与角色建立真实的情感羁绊。

【新关系：三位女性，三种命运】
她们不是同一种“女主模板”。有人代表过去，有人代表责任，有人代表诱惑与未知。你选择谁，也会伤害谁。

【新玩法：选择、记忆、关系、真相】
每一次选择都会影响角色关系、好感度、声望值与剧情走向。你可以赢得爱情，也可能输掉自己。

 

至于李洋最后会成为怎样的人，结局又是怎样的，我想把这个决定留给你。

about_html:
A Knight's Fury – The Vaults of Venom

A classic dungeon-crawling adventure inspired by the RPGs of the 80s and 90s, rebuilt for shorter, more replayable sessions.

Enter a world of deadly monsters, forgotten magic, hidden treasures, and ancient evil. Explore dangerous dungeons, master turn-based combat, collect powerful equipment, and grow stronger as you venture deeper into the unknown.

ONE ADVENTURER. NO PARTY.

You're not commanding an army or managing a party of adventurers. It's just you, your weapons, your potions, and whatever waits beyond the next door.

Experience old-school first-person dungeon crawling where exploration, preparation, and every decision matter. No unnecessary grinding or hundred-hour commitment—just adventure, danger, and discovery.

TURN-BASED, FACE-TO-FACE COMBAT

Your grandfather's new auto-sorting spell backfired.

Every potion in the apothecary tipped off its shelf. Every finished potion unravelled back into raw essence, and the loose colors pooled together in one enormous pile in the middle of the lab.

He chuckled. "Ah, it does that sometimes." Then he pulled on his coat for the annual Alchemists Gathering and asked you to mind the place while he is away.

He'll be gone about a month. There is no rush at all.

Two puzzles

Every potion needs two things done to it.

Decant. Pour the scrambled liquids from bottle to bottle until each one holds a single pure color. If you have ever played a water-sort puzzle, your hands already know this part.

Shelve. Carry the finished potion across the lab to the shelf it belongs on. Color gets you to the right wall. The sigil on its label picks the exact shelf.

You can only levitate a few bottles at a time, so the two puzzles compete for the same hands. Pour greedily and you have nothing free to carry with. Carry too much and you have nothing free to pour into. Deciding what to hold is the game.

One laboratory. 4,160 potions.

A gothic stone rotunda, two floors, tall arched windows and warm afternoon light. 52 shelved sections across thirteen families of potion.

Every one of the 4,160 potions is in that pile from the moment you start. Nothing respawns, nothing refills, nothing quietly re-stirs itself behind your back. The mess only ever gets smaller.

The room is the progress bar. The floor clears. The shelves fill and light up. A dark, dusty laboratory slowly becomes a glowing apothecary.

Relaxing is the whole point

No timers. No pressure. No penalties. No fail state. There is nothing here you can lose.

Warm window light, a quiet score, and the sound of glass and liquid. Put a potion on the wrong shelf and nothing scolds you. No buzzer, no shake, nothing taken away. Set a bottle down mid-pour, walk off, and come back next week to exactly where you left it.

Skills make the work easier. They never make it disappear.

Sorting earns XP, XP earns levels, and every level buys a skill point. There are 47 of them, across a board of 24 nodes.

A wider hand. A longer reach. Deeper buffers to work into, and sight that pulls a workable set out of the pile.

What none of them do is play for you. Nothing pours, carries or shelves on your behalf, and nothing sits on a cooldown. You get better tools and a bigger workspace. The satisfying part stays yours.

Three numbers, counted all the way down

52 sections. 364 shelf rows. 4,160 potions.

The game keeps all three counters and you can switch them on or off. No hidden progress and no rounding. Every potion you finish and shelve moves a number you can watch.

The lab is done when the pile is gone and all 52 cabinets are full. A finite game with a real ending, not a loop that farms you.
